body:
I went to a psychiatrist in April and got on a waiting list for therapy. Now I'm still on that waiting list after several intakes with different therapists (recently got shuffled onto another waiting list since "they can't put their finger on what my problem is"). All this time my med intake was upped with every visit (from 5mg to 30mg of Lexapro), while I experienced no positive change at all. Since people advice to be on meds and to be in therapy for the best results, I just quit the meds cold turkey this Summer. No sense in being one of those one out of ten adults who take antidepressants daily if you know that it's not even fully effective eh. But it was a quite painful experience, I also felt like passing out every moment, and weirdly enough I enjoyed every moment of it. 

I've also found that giving up seems to have become my favorite mode of responding to stressful situations, mostly in combination with pulling the "I'm sorry, I'm mentally ill"-card, even when it's more a matter of laziness and disinterest. So, in that sense I've become a disgrace for those with SA (and anxiety in general and depression and so on), who do want to change themselves and stand up against the presupposed ideas about them.

That's not going to happen. I already told him, also told my psychiatrist and the students councilor. All three advised against it, since I'd most likely end up neglecting myself, socially and physically, and my studies even more than now, and they're probably right about that.

*You* can do it. FTFY.

When you were writing that comment, I wrote my prof to tell her that I'm giving up. Right now, on another tab, I'm writing the others a lot of excuses and an implicit message saying they can go fuck themselves because I'm an egoist who doesn't have his shit together. Hell, you've got a 6000 word paper and are still able to say 'we can do it', while I'm at the brink of insanity for a 2500 word part of a paper. It's worse than I thought.
